speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To narrow this down, have you noticed any fever or chills accompanying the right flank pain? And when was the last time you passed blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis)

While your history of recurrent UTIs suggests possible infection, the classic presentation of visible hematuria combined with right flank pain is most indicative of a kidney stone. Did you notice any colicky pain that moved from your side to your groin, or did the pain remain localized to the flank?
